question.:question/problem: The curve has equation $x^{2} + 2 y^{2}=18$. The **tangent** line at $\left(-4,-1\right)$ meets the $y$-axis at $P$. Find the coordinates of $P$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Treat $y$ as a function of $x$. Differentiate implicitly and collect the derivative terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}
2 x+\left(4 y\right)\frac{dy}{dx}&=0 \\
\left(4 y\right)\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\left(2 x\right) \\
\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\frac{2 x}{4 y}
\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the given point:

$$
m_{\mathrm{t}}=-\frac{-8}{-4}=-2
$$

The tangent line uses $m=-2$.

Use the given point and this slope:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(-1\right)&=-2\left(x-\left(-4\right)\right) \\
y&=-2\left(x-\left(-4\right)\right)+\left(-1\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

At the $y$-axis, $x=0$. Substitute and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y&=-2\left(0-\left(-4\right)\right)+\left(-1\right) \\
y&=-9
\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore $P=\left(0,-9\right)$.

question.:question/problem: The curve has equation $3 x^{2} + y^{2}=21$. The **tangent** line at $\left(2,-3\right)$ meets the $x$-axis at $P$. Find the coordinates of $P$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Treat $y$ as a function of $x$. Differentiate implicitly and collect the derivative terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}
6 x+\left(2 y\right)\frac{dy}{dx}&=0 \\
\left(2 y\right)\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\left(6 x\right) \\
\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\frac{6 x}{2 y}
\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the given point:

$$
m_{\mathrm{t}}=-\frac{12}{-6}=2
$$

The tangent line uses $m=2$.

Use the given point and this slope:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(-3\right)&=2\left(x-\left(2\right)\right) \\
y&=2\left(x-\left(2\right)\right)+\left(-3\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

At the $x$-axis, $y=0$. Substitute and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}
0&=2\left(x-\left(2\right)\right)+\left(-3\right) \\
x-\left(2\right)&=-\frac{-3}{2} \\
x&=\frac{7}{2}
\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore $P=\left(\frac{7}{2},0\right)$.

question.:question/problem: The curve has equation $4 x^{2} + 2 y^{2}=72$. The **tangent** line at $\left(4,2\right)$ meets the $y$-axis at $P$. Find the coordinates of $P$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Treat $y$ as a function of $x$. Differentiate implicitly and collect the derivative terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}
8 x+\left(4 y\right)\frac{dy}{dx}&=0 \\
\left(4 y\right)\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\left(8 x\right) \\
\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\frac{8 x}{4 y}
\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the given point:

$$
m_{\mathrm{t}}=-\frac{32}{8}=-4
$$

The tangent line uses $m=-4$.

Use the given point and this slope:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(2\right)&=-4\left(x-\left(4\right)\right) \\
y&=-4\left(x-\left(4\right)\right)+\left(2\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

At the $y$-axis, $x=0$. Substitute and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y&=-4\left(0-\left(4\right)\right)+\left(2\right) \\
y&=18
\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore $P=\left(0,18\right)$.
